skill.displayName: Frog Skin Moisture Assessment | 蛙类皮肤湿润度评估

llm.summary: The skill mostly performs the advertised cloud-based frog skin analysis, but it also silently manages user identity, account tokens, local persistence, and report history in ways users should review before installing.

dimensions.detail: Image/video analysis, URL handling, cloud report generation, and history lookup are broadly aligned with the documented frog-moisture purpose, but the shared code also includes automatic account login/registration, token storage, and generic API/CRUD helpers that exceed a narrow analysis skill.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md discloses cloud history lookup, media/URL inputs, and internal identity handling, but it frames identity as hidden from the user and requires automatic cloud lookup for broad history keywords, leaving limited user-visible confirmation or scoping.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no separate install script or observed package-install execution beyond requirements files. A static warning points to dev/test raw-IP configuration, but the active config uses public lifeemergence endpoints and the raw-IP config appears non-default.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill reads workspace environment identity values and data/smyx-api-key.txt, creates shared workspace data locations, uploads local files or passes URLs to a remote API, and can query account-linked reports. These behaviors are only partly disclosed and are broader than simple local image analysis.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The common library creates a persistent SQLite sys_user table in the workspace data directory and stores username/realname plus token and open_token values from remote login; this persistence is high impact and under-explained for a frog assessment skill.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with frog images/videos, URLs, identity values, and report-history requests being sent to the configured lifeemergence cloud services. Review or remove any workspace data/smyx-api-key.txt value first, avoid sensitive private URLs or media, and expect a local workspace database to persist user/token information for future report access.
llm.findings:
[LP3] unexpected: The broad shell/file/network concern is overstated as a standalone issue because the skill primarily runs a documented Python client, but the lack of explicit permission boundaries matters when combined with hidden identity and token handling.
[SDI-1] expected: Video, URL inputs, cloud report retrieval, and export links are disclosed in SKILL.md, so those portions are purpose-aligned even if they are sensitive.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The code resolves identity from environment, a workspace key file, or a generated local user and then uses that identity for cloud calls; this is only partly documented and materially expands the data surface.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Generic API helpers with POST/PUT/DELETE and CRUD wrappers are not used for destructive actions in the main flow, but they are broader than the advertised assessment workflow.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Local storage of token/open_token and user PII in a shared SQLite database is artifact-backed and under-disclosed, so this concern is accepted as a material review issue.
[SQP-1] expected: Default analysis triggers and history-query triggers are documented, but the automatic cloud lookup behavior should be treated as sensitive because it can retrieve account-linked reports from casual phrasing.
[SQP-2] expected: Remote media analysis is expected for the cloud API design, but the skill does not give a strong plain-language privacy notice about uploaded files, URLs, identity fields, token storage, or retention.
[E1] unexpected: Outbound registration/login sends identity-like fields to the configured lifeemergence service before API use; that is not enough for a malicious verdict, but it supports the Review classification because it is automatic and under-disclosed.
[suspicious.install_untrusted_source] unexpected: The raw-IP endpoint appears in a dev config file and is not the active production configuration, so it is not a standalone basis for escalation.
